name: A claim attributed to another source, written as a fact

seen.corpus: Europe PMC JATS 2023-2026 (272 articles, the declared corpus)
seen.excerpt: MEASURED on 2026-09-15 by probes/2026-09/form-208-reported-claim.py, whose definition is in its docstring: 60/272 articles carry, in their body, a claim attributed to another source and written as a fact — « et al. also found that a greater proportion of visible green space in the community was associated with better cardiovascular health in older adults [CIT] » (bio-PMC12882215) — and in 7 of the 60 the next sentence denies or qualifies it (« et al. found that caffeine improved exercise performance in athletes with AA and AC polymorphisms though performance decreased in CC allele carriers », essai-PMC13239719). A reader that keeps the reported fact and drops its attribution asserts an edge the article never asserted; in the 7, one it denies. The strata: bio 16, essai 10, phys 9, meta 8, cas 7, moderne 6, nonEN 4.
seen.observer: Fault Atlas maintainer (Loxyn), by probe, no model

prevention.note: the attribution marker is detectable by rule (this probe: « et al. » or a citation, a reporting verb, « that »); whether code alone can re-anchor the claim to its source, or must abstain, is not assessed by the observer — to be classified by the second reader. Denial and reported speech were being fabricated in our test corpora with no observed form behind them; this is the form.

repair.note: a spurious edge is fully repaired by deletion once it is found; finding it needs the text, not the graph — the graph holds a well-formed edge with no mark of who asserted it
